llm.summary: The skill is a coherent local travel expense tracker, but its documented shell execution pattern can turn user-entered expense text into command execution and its filename handling is weak on Windows.

dimensions.detail: Local JSON persistence under `travel_expenses/` is expected for an expense tracker and disclosed, but the records can include sensitive travel and spending history.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hooks, dependency installation, remote payload retrieval, or package-manager behavior were found in the artifact files inspected.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs agents to run `python3 scripts/expense_tracker.py <tool> '<json_params>'`; interpolating user-controlled JSON into a single-quoted shell argument is unsafe when trip names or descriptions contain apostrophes or shell metacharacters.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script persistently reads and writes JSON files named from user-controlled trip names; only `/` and spaces are sanitized, leaving Windows backslash traversal and other unsafe filename cases insufficiently contained.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, script behavior, and bundled sample data align around recording travel expenses, budgets, categories, and summaries with no external network calls found.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use it only in an environment where local travel and spending records can be stored safely, and avoid running the documented command through shell string interpolation. The publisher should change the invocation to argument-array execution or stdin input, and harden trip-name path handling before broad use.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: the artifact itself documents shell-command execution with single-quoted JSON parameters, creating a command-injection risk if an agent follows that workflow with user-controlled fields.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted with scope limits: the script derives storage paths from trip names and does not reject Windows path separators or traversal components, so local JSON reads/writes may escape the intended folder on Windows.
[LP3] expected: Downgraded: local file persistence and Python script execution are disclosed and purpose-aligned, though the manifest/tool metadata is sparse and should scope filesystem access more explicitly.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly accepted as guidance: persistent local storage of travel expenses is central to the skill and disclosed, but users should understand the retention and privacy implications.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-language UX is obvious from the name, description, examples, script messages, and sample data; this is a usability/localization limitation rather than evidence of unsafe behavior.
